notes: Infrastructure as a service and stand-alone web hosting are not SaaS (r. 701-211.35; DOR guidance). Iowa's local option sales tax (LOST) is imposed on the same basis as the state sales tax (Iowa Code 423B.5), so one rule covers both; local hotel/motel taxes are separate and not modeled.

summary: In Iowa carpeting is never a building material: its sale is a taxable retail sale, and a lump-sum carpet-and-installation price is taxed in full. Other floor coverings attached to the floor are building materials, taxed to the contractor, not the customer.

conditions.when: Carpet and installation billed as one charge or lump sum
Carpet with the installation itemized separately, or under a separate contract: the carpet's price is taxed, the installation is not
Floor coverings other than carpeting, shaped to fit and permanently attached (building materials in a construction contract)

citations.title: Iowa Admin. Code 701—213.14, Carpeting and other floor coverings (IAC 2/5/25)
citations.quote: If the selling price of the carpeting and the installation charge are stated as one charge or lump sum, the entire charge is subject to sales tax.

citations.title: Iowa Admin. Code 701—213.14, Carpeting and other floor coverings (IAC 2/5/25)
citations.quote: The sale of carpeting is not to be treated as the sale of a “building material.”

notes: Added 2026-10-30 after held-out case ho-ia-07 showed the inherited construction.real_property.improvement rule was wrong for this code; the cited page is that case's source, so ho-ia-07 no longer counts as held out. Dated from the chapter's IAC date; the rule is older.
